lazy_mode_question.question: which of the five lazy modes is NOT covered by that cell
lazy_mode_question.answer: All five. The cell's promise is stated for allocating modes only, and it names the row's own non-allocating modes as outside it; none of the five lazy modes is asserted to print the class or to validate the scratch root. Verified: each of the five completes under an unusable TMPDIR with its expected exit and never even stats the scratch-root path (strace, zero references). Operationally: no `scratch_root` cell may be added to any lazy row - the counter's docs arm requires exactly seven such rows, so an eighth cell turns docs=7/7 into a failure. The exclusion to state by name is `context-capture --check`, because its tool is the one whose base `--selftest` printed the setup class on stdout; a reader could infer that `--check` prints the class too, and the cell says it does not.

findings.severity: routed, now measured by the amended counter
findings.what: `registry-check --rev` allocates the fleet-mirror clone through strict_scratch_root() (tools/registry-check.py:780) and was outside the counter's original eight modes. At HEAD it exited 2 with the class on stdout, non-grammar (`REGISTRY_CHECK: could-not-evaluate (cannot ...`), and `--rev --json` printed no class line at all. With the in-flight worktree fix both invocations print exactly one grammar-matching stderr line, rc 2, empty stdout.
findings.consequence: the counter was amended to nine allocating modes (note denominator = len(allocating)); the note now says nine and names `registry-check --rev`, and the registry-check cell names `--rev` in scope. If the worktree registry-check.py patch is dropped, the cell's --rev claim must be dropped with it.

findings.what: `repeat-control`'s refusal path writes `REPEAT_CONTROL: setup_error` to stdout (tools/repeat-control.py:232-234) while the frozen grammar line goes to stderr. The round's stated requirement is 'stdout carries no setup error'; the frozen counter checks stdout only for `RuntimeError`/`Traceback`, so it does not see this.
findings.consequence: a caller that keys on stdout sees a setup-error token; one line means one stream.

findings.what: The lane's in-flight tools/registry.json change is a whole-file re-serialization (1275 insertions / 1026 deletions) while the parsed rows are identical to HEAD outside the seven cells. This seat's patch is 7 changed lines.
findings.consequence: the L1 should apply a 7-line cell patch, not the re-serialized file.

findings.what: `/fast/scratch/hyaku/tameshi-r55/` was deleted while a 205 s counter invocation ran, destroying that run's receipts. Rebuilt; receipts are now written straight into the wave directory.
evidence: n/a - the deletion removed that run's outputs; the rebuilt evidence is receipts/c2-explain-ae76985.stdout

findings.what: c2/measure.py changed under the wave (denominator 8 -> 9, label fix, plain-run exit code with strace only for the mkdir census, normalized note matching). Cell text therefore carries no mode counts; the note cannot and had to move from eight to nine.
findings.consequence: sequence the note after the counter settles; quote a counter sha with every run.

findings.what: At C0 (9cf0146) four of the seven landed cells quote a line no tool prints: `repeat-control.py` (actual `repeat-control`), `bash-witness-study.py` (actual `WITNESS_STUDY`), `registry-check.py` (actual `registry-check`), `env-diff.py` (actual `ENVDIFF_SETUP`). The other three are correct. The counter's docs arm reads 7/7 because it only looks for the marker.
findings.consequence: apply cells-vs-c0.diff; the corrected text is validated against those same lines.

findings.what: Totals inside the amendment window run one above the deficits their receipts show: `7de93ea` printed total=3 with grammar=8/9 and note=8/9 (two shortfalls); `ee45944` and `51c315c` printed total=1 with every arm at its maximum and bad={}; `ae76985` printed total=0. Same receipts, different verdicts, so the extra point tracks the counter's own edits, not a measured arm.
findings.consequence: quote a launch-time counter sha with every run; if a deciding run lands in that window its verdict line and its receipt disagree, and the receipt is the better record.
